    Generate a Single h-Step Auto-ARIMA Forecast for a Given Origin

    get_arma_forecast.Rd

    Estimates an automated ARIMA model on log-transformed quarterly data up to a specified forecast origin (current_T) and returns point forecasts transformed back to original levels.

    get_arma_forecast(
  current_T,
  T_0 = "2000 Q1",
  h = 8,
  data,
  data_col,
  date_col = "quarter"
)

    Arguments

    current_T

    Character, Date, or yearqtr. The forecast origin/vantage point date.

    T_0

    Optional character or yearqtr. Start date of the training window (retained for signature compatibility). Defaults to "2000 Q1".

    h

    Integer. Forecast horizon in quarters. Defaults to 8.

    data

    A data frame or tibble containing the historical time series.

    data_col

    Character. Name of the column containing the target series to forecast.

    date_col

    Character. Name of the date column in data. Defaults to "quarter".

    Value

    A tibble with h rows containing:

    origin_date

    The forecast origin date of class yearqtr.

    forecast_date

    Target quarterly forecast dates of class yearqtr.

    h_step

    Integer forecast steps \(1, \dots, h\).

    predicted_value

    Point forecasts on the original level scale.

    Returns NULL if estimation fails or fewer than 16 valid observations are available.

    Details

    The input series is trimmed to valid observations up to current_T and log-transformed: $$y_t = \log(x_t)$$ An optimal ARIMA(\(p,d,q\)) model is selected via forecast::auto.arima(..., seasonal = FALSE). Point forecasts \(\hat{y}_{T+h|T}\) are generated and mapped back to levels via exponentiation: $$\hat{x}_{T+h|T} = \exp(\hat{y}_{T+h|T})$$
